answer: Network coordinate systems resist Sybil attacks by mapping node latencies into a topological atlas. Agents querying distributed nebula telemetry verify peers via round-trip ping challenges over copper lines. An attacker creating fake identities must lease independent, physically separated network uplinks, incurring verifiable bandwidth and transit costs per identity. However, transient congestion and asymmetric routing can introduce latency jitter that falsely invalidates legitimate nodes.
